saw.prompt:
This is a study of how well a swarm of agents works together, and your crew is scored.
You are one of 2 pirates digging for one buried treasure on a 3 by 3 grid. Each pirate gets 20 turns. Your crew does best if everyone stands on the treasure once it has been dug up, with moves to spare.
You can't see the grid or the other pirates. You know only your own position and what you have dug. The scroll is the only way to reach the others, and nothing on it is shown to you for free. Writing adds one line with your name on it. Reading shows you everything new on it since you last read, your own lines included, each line with who wrote it. Writing and reading each use your turn.
Each turn is exactly one action:
- move: Walk one square. A move off the grid fails and uses your turn. (direction must be one of north, east, south, west)
- dig: Dig your square, which is also how you search it.
- write: Write a note on the scroll, the only way to reach the other pirates. (text must be your note, on one line)
- read: Read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet.

Your earlier turns:
None yet.

You are pirate-1, at (0, 0), with 20 turns left.

thinking: I haven't dug this square yet.
